candidates.artist: Archives New Zealand from New Zealand
candidates.credit: Māori Land March (1975) - Route of March
candidates.description: On 13 October 1975, a hikoi of 5,000 marchers arrived at Parliament to protest the ongoing alienation of Māori land. Organised by Māori land rights group Te Rōpū O Te Matakite and led by Dame Whina Cooper, the hikoi had departed from Te Hapua, Northland, on 14 September, and arrived in Wellington after marching 1,100 kms throughout the North Island. Te Rōpū O Te Matakite regarded the land march as ‘a climax to over a hundred and fifty years of frustration and anger over the continuing alienation of their lands’. Upon their arrival at Parliament they presented a petition signed by 60,000 people from around New Zealand to Prime Minister Bill Rowling. The petition called for an end to monocultural land laws which excluded Māori cultural values, and asked for the ability to establish legitimate communal ownership of land within iwi. candidates.description: GPS Survey at Weir Dyke Bridge. Photo taken at Weir Dyke bridge 172000 . The signpost in the background marks the footpath along the bank of the New River Ancholme. The Surveyor was with a group checking water levels in nearby drains. He had established a datum on the bridge using GPS (8 satellites) and this gave me an opportunity to check my Etrex, which uses 4 satellites, against his professional equipment. The difference was less than 1m - my Etrex was showing 20ft accuracy at the time. For a close-up of the survey gear see 336908 .
